metadata.title: We visited the new Hickory's Smokehouse in Cambridge that boasts Deep South menu
metadata.contentSnippet: One of Cambridgeshire's newest restaurants opens its doors tonight, and diners are in for a finger-licking treat.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: We visited the new Hickory's Smokehouse in Cambridge that boasts Deep South menu
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: One of Cambridgeshire's newest restaurants opens its doors tonight, and diners are in for a finger-licking treat. Offering the taste of the American Deep South, Hickory's Smokehouse on Milton Road, Cambridge, does barbecue as you have never tasted before. We were invited to preview the restaurant, housed in the renovated former Milton Arms pub, on Wednesday evening. You are greeted by the smell of delicious smoky meat as you walk into the building, which is reminiscent of an old American bar in some Southern state, and it's enough to get those taste buds going. The Southern Sharer is just made for sharing, and the perfect starter. The venue has been completely stripped and refitted, with impressive results. Booths with upholstered seating and well-spaced wooden tables give diners a sense of comfort and privacy. The interior is rich in detail, helping create an authentic stateside feel. And the staff are some of the most welcoming I have ever encountered in any restaurant anywhere. My friends even commented on the warm welcome we received, and the enthusiasm of every staff member we encountered, from the friendly bartender to the waiting team. The evening let staff practise serving, the kitchen handle a packed restaurant and invited guests sample the menu, while families could use a cinema room showing children’s films with free popcorn. The entrance bar has the feel of a traditional saloon and serves drinks including Hickory’s own beers. Tailgator, a lager brewed in Scotland, is among them. The menu is packed with choice, including vegetarian and vegan dishes, but Hickory’s is primarily about the meat. And wow, what meat. There were four of us, and we were offered taster dishes of one of Hickory's specialities, slow-cooked smoked brisket, and it is to die for - simply melt-in-your-mouth delicious. The food was tasty, filling, and served with real Southern hospitality. We opted for a small starter, so we went for the Southern Sharer between three of us, and one of us chose the chicken in the basket as well. The platter came with bourbon-glazed smoked sausage, cowboy-buttered corn, smoked wings, celery, beer fondue and a selection of dips. Also on the platter were frickles, and if you have never tasted a frickle, then you have missed a treat. They are battered, deep-fried gherkins, and they are delicious. On to the mains, and we went for a variety. The interior of Hickory's Smokehouse, Cambridge has been designed with comfort and style. (Image: Neil Cooper) One of us chose the classic Gumbo - a hot and spicy southern stew served with rice, black beans and scallions alongside a baguette. It included smoked pulled chicken with pork, jalapeño, and cheese sausage. Verdict: hot, tasty and filling — ideal for stew lovers. Another of us chose the bird in the herd - Tennessee bourbon-gravy-glazed smoked beef baby back ribs, Kansas-style barbecue-sauced wings and cowboy buttered smoked chicken, all served with slaw and fries. The Gumbo was a tasty, hot treat and perfect for stew lovers. (Image: Hickory's Smokehouse) It was a mountain of food, but it went down a treat. A Hickory's Cobb salad with chicken was another choice, and this is like no salad you have had before. It combines crisp lettuce with Kansas caviar — black beans, sweetcorn, red and yellow peppers and spring onions — plus blue cheese, a soft-boiled egg, avocado and Cheddar. My friend found this a challenge to finish as it was so filling. Hickory's offers a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic cocktails, including a variety of Margaritas. (Image: Hickory's Smokehouse) Finally, I chose the Texas-style sliced brisket. If you think you have tasted brisket before, think again. This was smoked low and slow for 16 hours and served with a pot of bourbon gravy. It was utterly delicious, and just melted in the mouth - I can't recommend this enough. With the top buttons on our trousers already undone, it was time to move on to desserts, but we were so full there was only one option, and that was to share a couple of desserts between us. The bar area is a welcoming space as you enter the restaurant on Milton Road. (Image: Neil Cooper) We chose banana-pudding cheesecake in a jam jar and vegan ice cream. Shared between two, they were a fitting end to a filling but delicious meal.One of the highlights of the evening was the arrival at our table of a Pitmaster margarita cocktail. Served in a glass dome filled with smoke, it was one of the most theatrical drinks I've ever had. The designated driver tried a couple of the sodas, including the refreshing raspberry and mint, which was sweet and tangy and very refreshing. The Southern Sharer is just made for sharing, and the perfect starter. (Image: Sarah Cliss) Another of us tried the Sierra Nevada beer and said it hit the spot. Hickory's ethos is one of Southern hospitality, and the staff certainly delivered that on Wednesday evening; they were welcoming, chatty, and willing to please. A quick tot-up of our bill saw a total of around £140 without drinks, but for three courses, for four of us, and for the quality of the food, we thought it was worth it. Would we go again? Yes, definitely, but we may have to wait a while for the excess of the evening to go down first. Verdict: 5/5 for food, service and ambience - why not give it a try? The Cambridge branch is the second Hickory's to open in Cambridgeshire, following the Peterborough restaurant's opening in June.

metadata.title: St Ives extend unbeaten start with convincing win over Peterborough Lions
metadata.contentSnippet: St Ives maintained their unbeaten start with a comfortable victory over Peterborough Lions, despite a disjointed display in difficult wind.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: St Ives extend unbeaten start with convincing win over Peterborough Lions
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: St Ives maintained their unbeaten start with a comfortable victory over Peterborough Lions, despite a disjointed display in difficult wind. The league match took place at St Ives, although the day and scheduled time were not provided in the supplied report. Captain Dan De’Ath opened the scoring after a strong driving move had taken the hosts towards the line. For much of the opening twenty minutes, neither side found fluency as gusts made passes dip, spill and swerve in flight. Ives then tightened their attack, with Henri Cole and Torv Romeis crossing for tries in quick succession. Connor Newsome secured the try bonus point before half-time, stretching over with two defenders attached after the ball moved swiftly across the field. Charlie Mandley converted only one of the first-half tries against the wind, leaving the Bulls 22-0 at the interval. Cole added his second try early in the second half, forcing his way over after a quickly taken penalty. The match became scrappy for the next half-hour, with repeated handling errors and scrums reflecting both sides’ struggles to adapt to the conditions. The home defence nevertheless frustrated the visitors, while Ben Fleming dealt effectively with their kicking game and returned several balls well. As Peterborough tired, De’Ath completed his hat-trick with two late tries, before Josh Meadows finished the scoring with a fine solo effort after Mickey Drake took a quick tap. Mandley converted the late score and Ives secured a convincing win, although the performance never reached the heights suggested by the margin. Director of rugby Duncan Williams described the performance as disciplined rather than entertaining and welcomed another five-point haul. The result confirmed their unbeaten start after three rounds. The Bulls now turn their attention to next week’s encounter at St Neots, where they will seek to maintain their perfect league start.

The company that owns a Huntingdon hotel has submitted a planning application to build two covered padel courts on its grounds. Pinnacle Hotels Ltd has asked Huntingdonshire District Council for planning permission to build the courts at the Delta Hotels by Marriott site in Hinchingbrooke Business Park. The plans for Kingfisher Way include two semi-covered courts, sports lighting, glazed and mesh enclosures, landscaping and new pedestrian routes. Plans have been submitted to build two covered padel courts at the Delta Hotels by Marriott site in Kingfisher Way, Huntingdon. According to planning documents, the courts would be available to both hotel guests and members of the public and are intended to expand the hotel's leisure offering. Padel combines elements of tennis and squash and has surged in popularity, while the application says facilities remain limited in Huntingdon and across the district. The development would occupy part of the hotel's existing car park. Documents show the scheme would result in the loss of 16 parking spaces overall, reducing the total number from 226 to 210. However, a transport assessment submitted with the application concludes the remaining capacity would be sufficient to accommodate demand. Planning agents say the courts would improve health and recreation, support the local economy and boost the hotel’s appeal as a leisure destination. Supporting reports say the development would have little impact on neighbouring properties. A noise assessment found the facility would cause only a negligible increase in noise levels at the nearest home, approximately 140 metres away on Dyson Close. All boundary trees and hedgerows would be kept, apart from a dead silver birch that would be removed, the application says. Lighting would use downward-facing LED fittings designed to limit light spill beyond the site. The proposed courts would stand beneath a lightweight canopy designed to allow year-round use while remaining visually less prominent than a conventional indoor sports hall. The facility would be 9.5 metres high at its tallest point. Huntingdonshire District Council will decide the application later.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A Great Gidding bungalow can now be sold on the open market after planners lifted a decades-old agricultural occupancy restriction. Huntingdonshire District Council removed a condition restricting 91 Main Street, Great Gidding, to agricultural or forestry workers and their dependants. The restriction was first imposed when outline planning permission for the bungalow was approved in 1980. The home was built to provide accommodation for T B Trolove, who was an active partner in the family farming business. Planning documents submitted on behalf of the Estate of the late T B Trolove said the farming partnership has ceased active operations and is in the process of being wound up following Mr Trolove's death in January 2026. The application argued there was no longer a need for an agriculturally tied dwelling and that the surrounding area had changed significantly since the restriction was imposed more than 40 years ago. Planning officers backed the application, noting that the former farmyard next door had permission for up to eight homes and was no longer used for farming. Officers concluded the bungalow could no longer be regarded as an isolated rural dwelling and instead helped "round off" the built development at that end of the village. Great Gidding Parish Council raised no objections, and no members of the public responded before the application was decided. The council report said there was “no justifiable reason” to keep the restriction after the area changed and the farm business ended. Permission was granted on October 8, ending the agricultural tie and allowing the property to be occupied without restriction. The former farmyard redevelopment was first granted outline consent in May 2023, with the latest application seeking to replace that permission.

metadata.contentSnippet: Amazon opens £107m Peterborough distribution centre, creating 1,400 jobs.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A £107 million distribution centre has opened in Cambridgeshire, creating 1,400 jobs. Located in Peterborough, the new Amazon facility is the company’s first new building in the city in 15 years and is now the largest of its kind in Europe. The 690,000 sq ft site represents a major shift in Amazon’s logistics network, designed to store and distribute high-demand products to around 20 fulfilment centres nationwide rather than shipping items directly to customers. Staff at the new Amazon Peterborough site (Image: ©UNP Tim George) Tomislav Batinic, site leader at Amazon, said: "This site is a complete re-invention of how we run part of our logistics operation, and a historic moment for Amazon. "It is the first of its kind in the UK and the largest in Europe, and it is fitting that it is happening in Peterborough — a city with real history. "Products arrive from suppliers at one end and head out to fulfilment centres across the country at the other, all under one roof. "This type of site will be the template for how we run our operations in the years ahead, so it is a privilege to be the one introducing it. "We have called our team 'Team Founders' to mark how historic this moment is — and we are not just launching a building, we are laying the groundwork for something that will grow and endure long after Day One."

metadata.title: DWP State Pension age row deepens as 80,000 demand retirement at 65
metadata.contentSnippet: More than 80,000 people calling for the State Pension age to be cut to 65 have been dealt a blow after the Government confirmed it has no plans to lower it.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP State Pension age row deepens as 80,000 demand retirement at 65
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: More than 80,000 people calling for the State Pension age to be cut to 65 have been dealt a blow after the Government confirmed it has no plans to lower it. The petition is approaching the 100,000 signatures needed for Parliament to consider debating the issue. Supporters argue that people aged 65 to 67 can struggle to keep working because of ill health, caring responsibilities and limited job opportunities. For those forced to stop working early, the gap before their State Pension begins can be costly. Tim Grimsditch, managing director of financial advice platform Unbiased, said: “The Government has consistently rejected calls to lower the State Pension age, and the Third State Pension Age Review is currently underway to determine what the age should be in future decades. "There’s a difficult balance here: the State Pension is one of the largest items of public spending, and allowing people to claim it earlier would mean paying it to more people for longer. Both sides of this are serious arguments.” The petition can be viewed on the UK Parliament petitions website. The State Pension age is rising from 66 to 67, with the change due to finish in March 2028. It affects people born between March 1961 and August 1977. Legislation already exists for it to rise to 68 later. Private pensions can generally be accessed from 55, rising to 57 in April 2028. Anyone who stops working before claiming their State Pension may need to fund the gap themselves. Grimsditch said: “The practical issue for most people isn’t the State Pension age itself - it’s the gap before it. Private pensions can generally be accessed from 55, rising to 57 in April 2028, while the State Pension now arrives at 67. "Someone who stops working at 63 through ill health or caring responsibilities is funding four years entirely from their own provision. "That’s the question the petition is really about, and it’s worth planning for regardless of what happens to it.” The full new State Pension is £241.30 a week, or £12,547.60 a year. The amount people receive depends on their National Insurance record, so checking your State Pension forecast can help you understand what to expect. Grimsditch said: “It also matters because the State Pension alone was never designed to cover everything. The full new rate is £241.30 a week, or £12,547.60 a year, and what you actually receive depends on your National Insurance record.” Recommended reading Workplace and personal pensions, savings and investments can provide extra retirement income. Pension contributions can benefit from tax relief, while money held outside a pension can offer another source of funds. Grimsditch said: “Building additional income can mean a workplace or personal pension, where tax relief gives contributions a boost, or savings and investments held outside a pension. One change worth noting if you’re considering a cash ISA: the annual limit for under-65s falls to £12,000 from April 2027.” He urged people approaching retirement to review their finances and work out how much income they will need. He said: “If you’re within a decade of stopping work, the useful steps are checking your State Pension forecast, reviewing pensions you’ve accumulated along the way, and working out what income you’ll actually need. "Decisions about when to access a pension, how much to draw, and what to keep invested make a substantial difference to how long the money lasts - and that’s where a qualified financial adviser earns their fee. It’s never too early, or too late, to start.”

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A high street stationery store in Cambridgeshire is set to close as the retailer plans to end trading in the UK. Typo, owned by Australian group Cotton On, will close all its UK stores and end online trading by early 2027. As a result, the Typo store in Cambridge, located at 2 Lion Yard Shopping Centre, is set to close down in the next few months. A Cotton On Group spokesperson said: "After careful consideration we are closing Typo’s operations in the United Kingdom, with all stores and online trading to close by early 2027. "We recognise the impact of this decision on our Typo UK team who is already aware of this, and our priority is to support our people through this transition. "Over the past two years, we’ve taken steps to reshape Typo’s global operations and footprint to operate more sustainably, setting the brand up for a stronger long‑term future. "With the launch this year of our new Typo concept in Australia, South Africa and Malaysia, we’ve seen exciting momentum globally and remain incredibly optimistic about the brand’s future. "However, despite the efforts of our teams, ongoing high rent and operating costs, combined with softer sales, mean there is no sustainable path today for Typo in the UK. "Cotton On, Cotton On Body and Cotton On Kids will continue to operate through online and wholesale channels in the UK, and we remain confident in their long-term growth." The retailer, which launched in the UK in 2016, has operated stores in major shopping centres across the country, including London. A specific date for the closure of the Cambridge store has not been confirmed yet. The online store for UK customers is also expected to close by next year.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two men who attacked a group of boys before they stole a child’s bicycle in Peterborough have been convicted. Declan Hyland, 29, Imran Ali, 41, and another man ambushed the youngsters at about 5pm on April 18. They blocked the path of the teenage boys, two of whom were on bikes and the third a scooter, between Ivatt Way and Bourges Boulevard. They then pushed the boys off the bikes and repeatedly punched them, using keys held within their knuckles as improvised weapons. The boys tried to defend themselves, but Ali managed to ride off on one of the bikes - a Carrera worth about £600. He was closely followed by Hyland, who shouted an insult at the boys as he fled. The victims received minor injuries, including cuts caused by the keys that were used as weapons. Detectives reviewed CCTV footage from the area, resulting in Ali being identified and arrested. A media appeal was circulated with images of the two other men, resulting in Hyland being identified and arrested. The third man was not identified. Hyland, of no known address, admitted robbery and two counts of attempted robbery. Ali, also of no known address, denied the same counts but was found guilty following a trial at Cambridge Crown Court last month. On Monday (October 12) at the same court Hyland was jailed for five years. Ali will appear at Cambridge Crown Court on October 19 for sentencing. DC George Corney said: "This was a nasty attack on three teenage boys that understandably left them extremely shaken. "For three men to attack and rob a group of young boys, who admirably tried to defend themselves, really is cowardly. "I’d like to thank the public for helping us identify Hyland and therefore bringing him to justice." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Man dies after falling from bridge onto major A-road
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man has tragically died days after falling from a bridge onto a major A-road in Cambridgeshire. Police were called just after 12am on Monday (October 12) with a report of concern for a man who was stood on a bridge on the A11 at Chippenham. Cambridgeshire Constabulary said officers and other emergency services were deployed to the scene. However, at just after 1.30am the man fell and was rushed to Addenbrooke's Hospital in critical condition. In an update on Wednesday (October 15), the force confirmed the man had since "sadly passed away. "This will now be passed to the coroner." If you've been affected by the incident there is always someone to talk to. Call Samaritans on 116 123 from any phone for a confidential chat.

metadata.title: Woman arrested after 'tragic' death of baby girl 'detained in hospital'
metadata.contentSnippet: A major update has been issued on the "suspicious" death of a baby girl on Oxford Way, Cambourne.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Woman arrested after 'tragic' death of baby girl 'detained in hospital'
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A major update has been issued after the "suspicious" death of a baby girl in Cambridgeshire. Police were called at around 7.40pm on Saturday (October 10) with a report of concern for a woman and a property on Oxford Way, Cambourne. Officers attended and the baby was taken to Addenbrooke's Hospital, in Cambridge, but was sadly pronounced dead shortly after arrival. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the woman was taken to the same hospital and was arrested in connection. Speaking at the time, Detective Inspector Andy Moralee said: "This is a tragic death of a baby girl - a very sad and, we believe, isolated incident. "The circumstances remain under investigation, but we are treating her death as suspicious." In an update on Thursday (October 15), the force confirmed the woman is no longer under arrest and has been bailed and detained in hospital for further assessment. “A forensic post-mortem is due to take place on the victim tomorrow”. metadata.title: Limoncello confirms opening date for new St Ives restaurant and deli
metadata.contentSnippet: Limoncello restaurant in St Ives, Huntingdonshire, will open on November 5, offering authentic Italian food, a deli, garden and bistro.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Limoncello confirms opening date for new St Ives restaurant and deli
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: More details have been revealed about the opening of a new Huntingdonshire restaurant. Limoncello, which is currently located in Cambridge on Mill Road, announced in July this year that they would be expanding to St Ives. At the time, social media users shared their excitement. One commenter wrote on Facebook: "Very excited about this. Limoncello in Mill Road is exceptional!" Another said: "Looking forward to this as we now won’t have to travel to Cambridge!" Now, the business has confirmed when the new venue on Bridge Street will welcome its first customers. A grand opening event will take place on Thursday November 5 from 5pm. Limocello claims to offer "an authentic Italian experience" with a garden, deli and bistro. The business sources produce from Italian regions including Parma, Liguria, Campania and Modena. The Cambridge Limoncello menu features pizzas, antipasti, pasta dishes, steaks and salads accompanied by Aperol and Limoncello spritzes. The restaurant's website reads: "Our menus shift with the seasons, but our commitment to honest, regional cooking never changes. "Pair your meal with a glass of wine or one of our house cocktails…and always finish with a pour of our signature Limoncello."

metadata.title: Former RAF instructor 'honoured' after national business award nominations
metadata.contentSnippet: The founder of business Peterborough Blood Testing is "honoured" to be shortlisted as a finalist for the prestigious UK Small Business Awards.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Former RAF instructor 'honoured' after national business award nominations
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The founder of a Cambridgeshire blood testing business is "honoured" to be shortlisted as a finalist for prestigious national business awards. Peterborough Blood Testing, founded by mum, former PE teacher and RAF physical training instructor Emma Porsz, is a finalist in two categories at the 2026 UK Small Business Awards: Best Mobile Business and Best Business Startup. The Peterborough company takes private blood-testing and wellness services to clients’ homes and workplaces. Emma said: "I've always been into my health and fitness; I'm a PE teacher and I was a Physical Training Instructor (PTI) in the RAF. "I saw there was a bit of a gap in the blood testing market because I wanted a private blood test myself but I had to go to Cambridge or Leicester. "It was really difficult getting it on the NHS so I decided to set up a private mobile blood testing business." Emma Porsz founded Peterborough Blood Testing in 2026 Emma began working towards her qualifications in June 2026 and secured CQC registration. She has built the business gradually since the summer. She said: "People can book a blood test online - I have partnered with a lab - and they can book any blood test that they need. "Then I go to their home and take their test and get it sent off to a lab and they receive the results within 24 hours." Emma now offers platelet-rich plasma (PRP) microneedling and plans to add travel vaccinations, wellness injections and IV drips in November. She said she never expected the business to take off or earn an award nomination so soon after starting from scratch. Peterborough Blood Testing has been shortlisted for the UK Small Business Awards in two categories (Image: Emma Porsz) Emma said: "I feel really honoured and it's such an achievement for me. "I've actually handed in my notice at my current school and I'm going to be building it full-time and hope to expand it. It's very exciting." She runs the business alone but hopes to hire staff and expand into other cities. Building the business from scratch while working as a mum and PE teacher has been difficult but rewarding, she said. Emma said: "I'm loving it, going to people's homes, meeting new people and helping people. "It is a challenge but I really enjoy it."

metadata.title: Police investigating clash between councillors during controversial meeting
metadata.contentSnippet: Police have launched an investigation into a clash between two councillors during a controversial meeting of Huntingdonshire District Council.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Police investigating clash between councillors during controversial meeting
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Police have launched an investigation after a clash between two councillors during a controversial council meeting, it can be revealed. Cllr Stephen Ferguson clashed with Cllr Ryan Coogan at a full meeting of Huntingdonshire District Council on September 9. The incident occurred during a debate on a motion to review funds for plans to convert three cars parks into housing. Mr Coogan, the Reform councillor for Ramsey, objected after an amendment saw his motion cut from four pages to two. The pair clashed after Mr Ferguson, who chairs the district council, instructed Coogan to stop speaking and sit down. In a statement on social media shortly after the meeting, the chairman clarified his actions after "discussion online". The incident occurred during a debate on a motion to review proposals lodged by Capital and Centric (Image: Huntingdonshire District Council) "The member concerned had already spoken three times during the debate, more than any other member," he said. "At no point was I seeking to prevent them from speaking or expressing their views." Mr Ferguson claimed Mr Coogan's speech had strayed from the motion, breaching a council rule on debate. "I first tried, from the Chair, to remind the member to speak to the motion, an intervention which would have taken a few seconds," he added. "He simply continued speaking over me." Mr Ferguson said he stood during the debate, meaning the meeting had to fall silent, but Mr Coogan continued speaking over him. The meeting was subsequently adjourned. "I then resumed the meeting, returned to the Chair and, importantly, gave him the opportunity to continue his speech," he continued. "These are the same rules I had applied throughout the evening, and the same basic principles I have applied over many years of chairing councils at every level of local government. "They are there to ensure that debate is orderly, relevant and fair, and I will continue to apply them impartially." Cllr Coogan hit back on social media, claiming Cllr Ferguson had stopped him from “exposing the truth”. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed it was aware of the incident, adding it had received an online report. A spokesperson said: "An investigation is ongoing." Speaking to The Hunts Post, Ferguson revealed he hasn't been contacted by the force and is unaware of the allegations against him. He said: "I haven't been contacted by the police and have no idea what allegation is supposed to have been made about my conversation with Cllr Coogan. "It took place in a packed council chamber, in front of councillors, members of the public and the Council's Monitoring Officer. "I'll respond appropriately if I'm contacted by the police." In a statement, Huntingdonshire District Council said was aware that a referral has been made to police. "As this is an ongoing investigation, the council is unable to comment further at this time,” a spokesperson added. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: Princess Royal sees life-saving demonstrations at Cambridgeshire air ambulance base
metadata.contentSnippet: A royal visit has shone a spotlight on life-saving work in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Princess Royal sees life-saving demonstrations at Cambridgeshire air ambulance base
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A royal visit has shone a spotlight on life-saving work in Cambridgeshire. HRH The Princess Royal visited Magpas Air Ambulance’s headquarters in Alconbury Weald on September 29 for a special event celebrating lifesaving partnerships. HRH The Princess Royal, who officially opened the Magpas base in 2023 and has been a royal patron since 2020, met with clinicians, supporters, and emergency services partners. HRH The Princess Royal watched demonstrations of advanced skills and equipment Magpas Air Ambulance brings to the scene (Image: C1 Media) Daryl Brown MBE DL, CEO of Magpas Air Ambulance, said: "It was an honour to welcome Her Royal Highness back to the Magpas Air Ambulance base, having last visited to officially open the building, which has helped our advanced medical teams respond to more patients than ever before in recent years. "This celebration of lifesaving partnerships today highlighted the vital importance of partnership working, and acknowledged the professionalism, dedication and compassion demonstrated by all those involved in the responses to the Huntingdon and Bedford major incidents. HRH The Princess Royal speaking with Magpas Air Ambulance's Advanced Paramedics in Critical Care (Image: C1 Media) "We are always proud of our medical team members, who are there for our communities, families and loved ones, should the worst happen. "But also of the supporters who are vital to enabling the medical team to respond when every second counts. "We’re truly grateful for HRH The Princess Royal’s recognition of everyone who helps to save lives and for her wonderful support of Magpas Air Ambulance." HRH The Princess Royal addresses attendees at Magpas Air Ambulance's headquarters (Image: C1 Media) The event brought together those involved in recent emergency responses, including the Bedford train collision and the incident at Huntingdon station. Magpas was the first medical resource on scene in Huntingdon and the first air ambulance service to land at the Bedford train collision. HRH The Princess Royal met emergency services partners from across the region who work together at the scene of major incidents  (Image: C1 Media) During her visit, The Princess Royal observed real-time demonstrations of advanced treatments delivered by the Magpas clinical team and learned more about the charity’s efforts to train communities in bystander CPR.

metadata.title: Rare King Charles 50p sells for more than 200 times its face value
metadata.contentSnippet: Only 200,000 were released into banks and post offices, making it the rarest 50p in active UK circulation

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Rare King Charles 50p sells for more than 200 times its face value
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A rare 50p coin has fetched more than 200 times its face value after an online auction. The Atlantic Salmon piece drew 37 bids on eBay before being snapped up for £123. Released by the Royal Mint in 2023, only 200,000 copies of the coin were ever produced. The coin celebrates British wildlife and the accession of King Charles III, depicting the Atlantic salmon as a priority conservation species in UK waters. King Charles Salmon 50p sells 8 times face value. (Image: eBay) The reverse features a leaping Atlantic salmon alongside the King Charles III royal cypher, while the obverse bears the official uncrowned portrait of King Charles III by Martin Jennings. It is officially ranked by the Royal Mint as the rarest 50p coin in active UK circulation, having ended the 15-year reign of the 2009 Kew Gardens 50p. With just 200,000 released into banks and post offices, finding one in loose change remains exceptionally rare. The 50p piece provides a distinct heptagonal canvas for coin designers. With a diameter of 27.5mm, it is the largest British coin in circulation and offers space for commemorative artwork. Rarity serves as the primary factor driving collector demand and market prices. Low mintage figures mean fewer examples exist to buy or trade. Coin condition also plays an important role, with well-preserved specimens securing higher prices. Collectors also prize unusual design errors and striking flaws that escape the mint. Sales avenues can influence the price realised for a rare coin. Sellers often turn to competitive online bidding on eBay to test market demand. Others prefer formal valuations from professional coin dealers to establish a certified market value. Royal Mint mintage figures confirm the rarest 50p designs to enter general circulation: The 2023 Atlantic Salmon coin holds the title as the rarest 50p design in circulation. Anyone checking their loose change is urged to keep an eye out for these scarce editions.

metadata.title: New busway approved between Waterbeach and Cambridge
metadata.contentSnippet: A new busway linking Waterbeach New Town with Cambridge has been approved despite fears that issues with current routes are “damaging public trust”.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New busway approved between Waterbeach and Cambridge
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A new busway has been approved despite fears that issues with current routes are “damaging public trust”. The Waterbeach to Cambridge Transport Scheme (W2C) will create a new guided busway route linking Waterbeach New Town with Cambridge. Cllr Anna Bradnam, county councillor for Waterbeach, said the project had been “a long time” in the works and many concerns had been “worked through and resolved”. The Lib Dem councillor said she thought it would be “an extremely important transport link to Cambridge” which is needed with the 11,000 planned homes in the new town. Cllr Darren Green, of Romsey, said he saw “both sides of busways” as either “value-for-money mass transit” or a “cut-price solution”. The Green councillor said: “As far as I can see, there’s not been any progress in trying to solve the problem of how buses may progress through the rush-hour traffic in the morning. Our busways will essentially just hit the same traffic that everyone else is stuck in as soon as they reach Cambridge. “I think now is the time to really question whether Cambridge deserves a better solution for its public transport issues than busways.” Cllr Alex Bulat, of St Ives South and Needingworth, said she would vote for the motion but warned existing busways must be improved to “restore public perception”. The Labour councillor said the Cambridge to St Ives route is “sadly, not currently a success anymore” as it’s “not a commercially viable route”. She said: “What happens on the ground is actually damaging public trust in this type of public infrastructure. “Because people in St Ives, and beyond, face endless delays to travel, commuters are going back to their cars day after day.” Cllr Rory Clark, of Castle, said the busway would give young people and those who don’t drive the ability to move around the county. The Lib Dem councillor said: “I’m sure we would all love a fully fledged light rail system around Greater Cambridge and, indeed across the whole county, but we have to be realistic about the money we have on the table. “Letting the perfect be the enemy of the good isn’t a reason to further exclude young people in Cambridgeshire.” Cllr Alex Beckett, chair of the highways and transport committee, said there was “no shortage of ideas” for public transport in Cambridgeshire. The Lib Dem councillor said: “The most frustrating thing about this is everyone with their own idea nearly always wants to vote against someone else’s idea because it might mean that their idea then becomes less successful. “It just goes round and round in circles – everyone knows that we need to do something and I think that is the really important thing. Making sure that we really do start addressing the issues rather than kicking the issues into the long grass.” The council approved the scheme with 40 votes in favour, eight against and seven abstentions.

metadata.title: Controlling partner jailed for 'appalling' campaign of abuse against ex
metadata.contentSnippet: A Whittlesey man has been jailed for an "appalling" campaign of abuse against his ex-partner, including violence, threats, and coercive control.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Controlling partner jailed for 'appalling' campaign of abuse against ex
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man has been jailed for an "appalling" campaign of abuse against his ex-partner, including violence, threats, and coercive control. Leonard Evans, 35, of Richardson Way, Whittlesey, began dating the victim in November 2024 and quickly became controlling. He demanded the relationship be made public on social media just one week after meeting, and when she refused, he became angry. Evans monitored her phone, deleted male contacts, controlled her appearance and regularly accused her of cheating. He also made her feel unable to leave the house or socialise. While in prison for a previous conviction, Evans repeatedly called the victim from custody. After his release in February 2025, Evans accused her of cheating, then punched and strangled her until she could not see. During another attack, he pulled her hair and rammed her head into a wall. Leonard Evans made the victim feel unable to leave the house or socialise (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) He also threatened to burn down her home and her friend’s. During a day out in July, Evans verbally abused her and punched her in the head while she was driving. He was arrested and later pleaded guilty to coercive control, intentional strangulation, assault by beating, and threatening to damage or destroy property. On Friday, October 9, Evans was jailed for two-and-a-half years at Peterborough Crown Court and given an indefinite restraining order. Detective Constable Maisie Pratt, who investigated the case, said: "Evans’ sustained threatening, abusive, and violent behaviour was absolutely appalling and the level of manipulation he showed towards the victim is truly shocking. "He tried to control all aspects of her life and made her feel as though she was trapped. "I would like to commend the victim for her courage in coming forward and for her bravery throughout this whole process. “Domestic abuse can take many forms and often escalates quickly. "If you or someone you know is experiencing violence or controlling behaviour, please know that support is available and we will always take reports seriously.” For advice, support or to report domestic abuse, visit the force’s dedicated web pages.

metadata.title: Horror play 'fails to deliver a genuinely chilling experience' says Cambs reviewer
metadata.contentSnippet: We went to the Peterborough performance of Blackout: Fear Loves An Audience and this is what we thought.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Horror play 'fails to deliver a genuinely chilling experience' says Cambs reviewer
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: We went to Blackout: Fear Loves An Audience, which was marketed as a hauntingly immersive theatrical experience, and this is what we thought During its recent run at The New Theatre in Peterborough, the play attracted an audience anticipating a high-impact, two-act horror experience. The set design was ominous, establishing a chilling atmosphere before the show began. A flickering ghost light, a prominent ticking grandfather clock and as the thick stage smoke cleared, a centrally positioned chair equipped with handcuffs came into view. Before anyone could discuss what could be seen, the theatre was plunged into darkness, promoting a palpable reaction from the stalls. The production placed the audience as silent observers of actors rehearsing the play "The Devil's Daughter" within an old haunted venue. The reliance on the venue's existing environment to create immersion 'pulling you into to the play itself' proved ineffective, particularly given the theatre’s modern refurbished building. The play itself, which evolves to reveal the actors' own ghostly experiences, is slightly comical, yet the script relied heavily on profanity to achieve it's intended impact. While the production had the potential to deliver significant suspense, it ultimately failed to achieve the objective. The post-show feedback suggested that the experience did not meet the expectations of those seeking a genuinely chilling performance.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Fresh plans have been submitted to turn a former RAF Association club into new homes after a previous application was refused. OTAA St Neots Property Ltd wants to convert the Grade II-listed building at 44-46 Huntingdon Street, St Neots, into eight homes and build a three-bedroom house at the rear. The move comes after similar plans were refused earlier this year. In February 2026, the council turned down proposals for the conversion of the building into seven homes, alongside the construction of two bungalows at the rear. Before the refusal, planning officers had raised concerns about harm to the listed building and conservation area, flood risk, privacy and inadequate waste storage. That application hoped to restore the property back to its historical use - a series of residential units called The Limes. Similar plans for the club were refused by the council in February Later, the building became established as a pub for the town's Royal Air Force Association. The private members club closed its doors in 2023 after declining membership, and the building was handed back to RAFA, standing vacant ever since. The new plans would restore and convert the historic building into eight homes, with a detached house at the rear. There are also plans for landscaping works, parking facilities, cycle storage, and drainage improvements. The new plans involve creating eight homes within the existing building and a detached home at the rear A heritage assessment submitted with the application concludes the proposals would cause "less than substantial harm" to the listed building but argues this would be outweighed by public benefits, including restoring the deteriorating asset and securing its long-term future. The design team says the scheme would improve the building with repairs to its windows, roof and exterior finishes. New landscaping would replace much of the existing hardstanding, with private gardens, hedgerows and trees added across the site. Five more car parking spaces would be added according to the plans, bringing the total number at the site to 11. There are also 24 new cycle spaces proposed. Full details on the application can be viewed using the Huntingdonshire District Council planning portal.

metadata.title: More than 5,500 EV charge points planned across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
metadata.contentSnippet: Thousands of new electric vehicle charging points are set to be installed across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: More than 5,500 EV charge points planned across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Thousands of new electric vehicle charging points are set to be installed across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. The £5.4 million project, funded through the Government’s Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (LEVI) scheme, will deliver more than 5,500 charge points across the region, with 1,058 planned for Peterborough. Paul Bristow, Mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, said: "Our commitment to delivering 930 chargers is unlocking many more times that number, which is exactly what I want our funding to do. "If you've got a driveway, charging an electric car is more straightforward. "If you haven't, it's been a real barrier, so this funding will help put EV charging within reach for more people." The scheme is designed to support residents without off-street parking by providing accessible charging options close to home. The chargers will be installed on residential streets and will include two sockets per unit. A 15-year contract has been awarded to Believ by Peterborough City Council. In Cambridgeshire, 4,527 charge points will be installed, while Peterborough will receive 1,058. Councillor Angus Ellis, cabinet member for environment at Peterborough City Council, said: "This is a significant chance to accelerate our city’s transition to cleaner, greener transport whilst improving access to EV charging for residents who do not have off-street parking. "The move ties in with our ongoing work to reduce carbon emissions and we will use grant funding to unlock substantial private sector investment, delivering a much larger and more accessible charging network than could be achieved through public funding alone." The project supports the region’s 2040 target of ensuring 80 per cent of households without off-street parking are within a five-minute walk of a public charge point or able to charge on-street from a domestic charger. Delivery of the new infrastructure is planned to begin in 2027, subject to the remaining statutory procurement stages.

metadata.title: Warnings of ‘incredibly serious’ water shortage if supply concern not taken seriously
metadata.contentSnippet: Warnings have been raised that Cambridgeshire could face an ‘incredibly serious’ water shortage if supply concerns are not taken seriously.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Warnings of ‘incredibly serious’ water shortage if supply concern not taken seriously
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Warnings have been raised the region could face an ‘incredibly serious’ water shortage if supply concerns are not taken seriously. South Cambridgeshire District Council raised the alarm after it emerged a water credits system is no longer being actively progressed. The £4.5m scheme was announced in 2024 to offset the pressure on Cambridgeshire’s water network caused by new housing developments. At a scrutiny meeting last month, representatives of the newly-launched Greater Cambridge Development Corporation said they were still working on “what shape” the system could take but it was not being “actively progressed”. Cllr Dr Richard Williams said:  “I think we were all very surprised to hear that the water credits system is no longer a priority for the water scarcity group. “We should make it very clear that the water shortage in Greater Cambridge is incredibly serious. “We all saw it in the summer with the drought that we experienced. “If we have another few summers like that I think Greater Cambridge could have a very serious water problem. But we can all see the impact on the natural environment around us.” “We need really serious action – we need it now.” The Conservative councillor asked South Cambridgeshire District Council to support a motion expressing “alarm” at recent statements made “from more than one agency” which suggest “water supply is no longer regarded as an immediate concern in Greater Cambridge”. Cllr Chloe Wills-Eve asked how this could be the case while a hosepipe ban which came into effect in July is still ongoing. The Liberal Democrat councillor said: “How can water no longer be considered an immediate concern when existing residents are being asked to restrict their own usage? “I’m not opposed to development but it must be sustainable. “Before planning powers transfer to the Dev Co we need clear answers and a credible, deliverable plan.” Cllr Laurence Damary-Homan said: “I don’t even know how I can go about describing what I felt when I heard the development corporation’s comments on water in this area. “Every single one of us in this room knows how serious an issue this is.” The Liberal Democrat councillor said it was “beyond belief” that they were not taking water supply issues as “seriously as they need to be”. Cllr Anna Bradnam said it was “extremely worrying” that the development corporation was no longer treating the credits scheme as a priority. The Liberal Democrat councillor said: “Water credits was the way our concerns about water supply were going to be answered. “That was to give us comfort to cover the decisions that we were making as planning committees. “I think it’s going to be difficult for us to make decisions going forward.” Cllr Heather Williams said they were unable to object to planning applications based on water supply because the credits system was promised. The Conservative councillor said: “It does make me think what’s happened to those planning consents that are already out there, that were made on the basis of water credits coming through. “What this council has done, unintentionally, is made an already very difficult situation worse because of the lack of accurate information that was given at the time. “Everyone needs to try and really emphasise the need to sort this out quickly and we also need the backup to be able to say no to development if these matters are not resolved.” The motion passed unanimously.

metadata.title: Flagship Drive Project launched to tackle high-risk domestic abuse in Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: A flagship scheme is being rolled out to reduce domestic abuse in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Flagship Drive Project launched to tackle high-risk domestic abuse in Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A flagship scheme is being rolled out to reduce domestic abuse in Cambridgeshire. The Drive Project, launched through a multi-agency partnership, will focus on changing the behaviour of high-risk perpetrators across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. Darryl Preston, police and crime commissioner for Cambridgeshire, said: "Victims are at the heart of everything I do as Commissioner. "The roll out of this flagship project will support the work already underway across Cambridgeshire to manage risk and break the cycle of abuse to protect victims and ensure perpetrators are rightly held accountable for their actions." The programme will be delivered by Red Snapper Managed Services and is supported by Cambridgeshire County Council, Peterborough City Council, Cambridgeshire Constabulary, and the Probation Service. Case managers will work one-to-one with high-risk perpetrators over several months, aiming to change their behaviour through close monitoring and disruption tactics. The scheme will take a tailored approach based on individual risk levels and will involve co-ordinated action across multiple agencies. Survivors will also benefit from additional support, with two new posts created to strengthen the work of independent domestic violence advisor (IDVA) services in the county. The project is funded by the Home Office following a successful bid by the commissioner’s office. It forms part of the government's Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) Strategy. Jonathan Hussey, managing director of Red Snapper Managed Services, said: "We are proud to have been chosen to deliver the Drive Project in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. "Drive holds the people causing harm to account, disrupting their behaviour and, wherever possible, changing it for good. "Our team will be working with the highest-risk individuals in the county, and we look forward to seeing the difference we can make alongside local services." Perpetrators will be identified and referred to the scheme via multi-agency arrangements.

metadata.title: New Milton police station opens with 24-cell custody suite and modern facilities
metadata.contentSnippet: A new police station has officially opened in Milton.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New Milton police station opens with 24-cell custody suite and modern facilities
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A new police station has officially opened in Milton. Located next to Milton Park and Ride, the two-storey facility is designed to improve public services, manage growing demand, and support officers and staff with modern infrastructure. It replaces the outdated Parkside Police Station. Chris Balmer, Chief Constable of Cambridgeshire Constabulary, said: "The opening of Milton Police Station is a significant moment for Cambridgeshire Constabulary and for the communities we serve. Officers and staff have moved into the purpose-built police station (Image: Cambridgeshire Constabulary) "This modern, purpose-built facility gives our officers and staff the environment, tools and capacity they need to meet rising demand, respond more efficiently, and provide a high-quality service to the public for many years to come. "It represents a major investment in community safety and in our frontline people." The station includes a 24-cell custody suite—double the previous capacity—alongside interview rooms, medical facilities, and secure holding areas. It also features open-plan offices, space for investigative work, and areas for cross-force and multi-agency collaboration. Sustainability features include air source heat pumps, solar panels, and electric vehicle chargers. The building has achieved an A rating for energy efficiency. Darryl Preston, Police and Crime Commissioner, said: "As a former police officer who regularly worked out of Parkside Police Station, the Milton facility offers a more modern working environment for police officers and staff. The new station includes a 24-cell custody suite and modern facilities (Image: Cambridgeshire Constabulary) "It’s better access to our roads network will enable the Constabulary to meet the demands of our growing population, particularly in the south of the county. "I would like to thank everyone involved in the development – from the constructors, Wilmott Dixon to our Estates and IT Team who have worked tirelessly to make this happening." Plans for the new station were submitted in September 2020. Following an archaeological investigation, construction started in January 2024. The new facility replaces Parkside Police Station, built in the 1960s.

metadata.title: UK destination named among 'fastest-growing' travel spots for 2027 in new report
metadata.contentSnippet: Escapism, adventure and a touch of nostalgia are set to shape the way we travel.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK destination named among 'fastest-growing' travel spots for 2027 in new report
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Escapism, adventure and a touch of nostalgia are set to shape the way we travel, according to a new travel trends report. Expedia and Hotels.com have launched their latest travel trends report, Unpack '27: The Trends in Travel, revealing the top destinations and emerging travel behaviours expected to define 2027. The report combines first-party data, a survey of 26,000 travellers and social listening to identify a shift towards more intentional, personalised journeys. Ariane Gorin, chief executive of Expedia Group, said: "Travel is about creating memories, and Unpack '27 uncovers the destinations and experiences shaping those moments. "In 2027, travellers are being more intentional in choosing their next adventure, seeking experiences that are more personal and purposeful to them. "We’re making it easier to discover, plan and book the right trip, so travellers can spend less time managing the details and more time enjoying the moments that matter." Among the fastest-growing destinations globally, Chichester in the UK featured on Expedia’s 2027 Destinations of the Year list, alongside South Lake Tahoe in California, Hyogo in Japan, and Punta del Este in Uruguay. The report highlights the growing appeal of “Un-Adulting” getaways—child-free escapes packed with playful, nostalgic activities. More than half of travellers (57%) said they are likely to book such a trip in 2027, rising to 711% among Gen Z and Millennials. British travellers described these experiences as "having fun and enjoying a carefree day out" (74%), a way to spend "quality time with loved ones" (64 per cent), and a break from "everyday responsibilities" (60%). Hotels.com identified a surge in “Trip Snacking”—short, one-night stays designed to fit around busy schedules and limited budgets. Nearly eight in 10 travellers (79%) plan to book a one-night stay in the coming year, with numbers rising to 83% among younger generations. For British travellers, top reasons for these mini-breaks include attending concerts or sporting events (49%), celebrating milestones (42%), or simply needing a quick reset (23%). Atmosphere is becoming increasingly important, with 56% of travellers booking hotels for their atmosphere or aesthetic appeal. A growing number (65%) are specifically interested in “Gothic Getaways”—dramatic, moody stays featuring neo-Gothic architecture, castles and dark, immersive interiors. These experiences are especially popular among Gen Z and Millennials, with 71% expressing interest. Social media mentions of Gothic architecture and travel have risen by 38%, and global demand for castle properties on Hotels.com has grown by 20%. Film and television continue to influence the way we travel, with nearly one in five travellers booking trips to destinations featured on screen. UK respondents reported spending an average of £600 on these “Set-Jetting” trips, with the figure rising to £629 for those travelling with children. New seasons, sequels and franchise extensions mean that this travel trend is likely to continue well into 2027. Almost half of travellers surveyed said they had researched or booked trips to locations from upcoming shows or films, a figure that jumps to 58% among younger travellers. Expedia’s 2027 trend report paints a picture of travel that is increasingly playful, purposeful and influenced by the worlds of entertainment and design.

metadata.title: UK households could be owed up to £180 TV Licence refund - how to claim money back
metadata.contentSnippet: UK households who do not watch live TV or BBC iPlayer could claim a TV Licence refund of up to £180, while over-75s could get a free licence.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK households could be owed up to £180 TV Licence refund - how to claim money back
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Households who do not watch live television could claim a TV Licence refund of up to £180. Anyone with a valid licence who no longer watches live broadcasts or BBC iPlayer can apply to cancel their cover and get money back. TV Licensing calculates refunds based on the number of complete unused months remaining before the licence expires. Applicants must have at least one full month left on their licence to qualify, meaning refunds can cover between one and 11 months. Official guidance states: "Any refund due is calculated in unused months. You must have at least one complete month left on your licence that you won’t need before it expires. "So, you could get a refund for between one and 11 months, depending on how long you have left on your licence." TV Licensing aims to process and issue approved refunds within 21 days of receiving an application. Payments are issued either by cheque or directly into a bank account through a BACS transfer. Households cannot claim a refund if there is less than one month between the cancellation date and the expiry date. A TV Licence is legally required to watch or record live television on any channel or service, including Freeview, Sky and Virgin Media. Cover is also required to watch live programmes on streaming services such as Amazon Prime Video, ITVX, YouTube and Netflix. Anyone using BBC iPlayer must also hold a licence, whether watching live, catch-up or on-demand content. Viewers do not need a licence to watch on-demand programmes on services like Netflix, Disney Plus or Amazon Prime Video, provided they are not broadcast live. Watching DVDs or on-demand clips on video websites without live broadcasts also does not require a licence. Households may also qualify for a free TV Licence if someone living at the address meets specific criteria. Residents aged 75 or over who receive Pension Credit can claim a free licence rather than paying the annual fee. Guidance from TV Licensing confirms: "Free TV Licences are only available if you’re 75 or over and you, or your partner living at the same address, are receiving Pension Credit." Eligible residents can apply online or by calling 0300 790 6117 between 8.30am and 6.30pm on weekdays to request a paper form. Those applying for a free licence do not need to cancel their existing Direct Debit, as TV Licensing will cancel payments automatically and issue any refund owed.

metadata.title: Further details surrounding tragic death of man hit by coach revealed
metadata.contentSnippet: Further details of the events leading up to the tragic death of a man hit by a coach on the A14 between Histon and Milton have been revealed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Further details surrounding tragic death of man hit by coach revealed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Further details surrounding the tragic death of a man hit by a coach on the A14 in Cambridgeshire have emerged. Nathan Price, 33, of King's Hedges Road, in Cambridge, died after he was struck by a white Yutong coach on September 12. The crash occurred on the eastbound carriageway of the A14 between Histon and Milton at around 1.35pm. Mr Price was tragically pronounced dead at the scene (Image: National Highways) According to Cambridgeshire Police, a 39-year-old man from Peterborough, who was driving the coach at the time of the collision, was uninjured. The crash, near Cambridge, shut the eastbound carriageway for several hours, with motorists urged to avoid the area. In a tribute, Mr Price's family said: "In loving memory of Nathan Ellis Price, a very much-loved son, brother, father and uncle. "Nathan was a kind, loving person with the biggest heart and has left a very big void in our hearts." The driver of the coach was uninjured (Image: National Highways) An inquest was opened into the 33-year-old's death by coroner Elizabeth Gray at Vantage House, in Huntingdon, on Thursday (October 8). The brief hearing revealed Mr Price suffered traumatic injuries to the head, spine, thorax, abdomen, pelvis and extremities. An inquest has been scheduled for April 1, 2027. metadata.title: East Anglia awards spotlight sustainability champions and educational trailblazers
metadata.contentSnippet: Meet the judges for the Clean & Green Champion and Educational Trailblazer categories at the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: East Anglia awards spotlight sustainability champions and educational trailblazers
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The East Anglia Clean & Green Awards are all about putting the spotlight on the people who are working to make our region a leader in sustainability. The judges for both the Educational Trailblazer Award, which is currently open for entries, and the Clean & Green Champion Award – the winner of which will be selected by a panel of judges – are looking for those unsung heroes who are helping our communities shine. Here, we find out more about the qualities that the judges will be looking from candidates. Sponsored by RWE Sponsor judge: Edward Robb, stakeholder manager, RWE Edward Robb is stakeholder manager at RWE, which sponsors the Clean & Green Champion Award (Image: Edward Robb) Why were you keen to get involved in the Clean & Green Awards? Sustainability is at the heart of everything RWE does as a pioneer of clean energy technologies. We love to support the local community in East Anglia and champion those that share our values of driving the energy transition and sustainable practices. What do you bring to the judging panel for the Clean & Green Champion Award? In my role on the Vanguard and Boreas wind farms, I am privileged to meet lots of people at the heart of their communities. I love to see a blend of community values and sustainability, in local communities and within the business community as well. What will you be looking for in the winner? Community is at the heart of everything RWE does in East Anglia, and we want to see incredible examples of those committed to their communities, supporting and engaging with them on multiple levels and recognising the importance of community to the region. We want to see the individuals that drive this commitment to community and how their passion and efforts help to further our community. What advice would you give to local businesspeople who want to be recognised at these awards? Showcase the individuals behind your work and show us the creative and innovative ways in which you are driving sustainability within your community. What do you expect to see in terms of community impact? Being able to bring a community together around a project, business or organisation is an incredible feat, especially when tied to sustainability. Sponsored by East Coast Energy Training Academy Rachel Bunn, director, East Coast Energy Training Academy Rachel Bunn is a director at East Coast Energy Training Academy, which sponsors the Educational Trailblazer Award (Image: East Coast College) Can you tell us a bit about your career to date? I have worked at the college in a variety of roles, starting in 2001, but skills and innovation is at the heart of my work. I am also the college STEM lead and CSR (corporate social responsibility) champion. A key aspect on my work is supporting individuals and communities to explore how training can help recruitment and retention. Why were you keen to get involved in the Clean & Green Awards? We need to shout about the great work that is taking place in the region. The awards support companies and showcase why they deserve this award outside of what they do in their day job. What do you bring to the judging process? Challenge, rigour and passion, with an understanding of what makes amazing ideas come to life. Have you ever been judged for an award yourself? If so, how will you use that experience when judging this award? I have been judged for awards recognising community impact as well as staff awards. This experience gives me clear guidance and reasoning when assessing entries, as well as an understanding of how nominations should describe and explain what makes them stand out. What will you be looking for in the winner? The ability to explain what, why and how. The winner’s story needs to have glitter, fireworks, something really special that helps it stand out from the crowd. What advice would you give to anyone that’s considering entering? Why not! By entering these awards, you have the opportunity to showcase why and how you have gone above and beyond to the whole region! The deadline for entries to the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards is Sunday, November 8 at midnight. For more information, or to enter, please visit cleanandgreenawards.co.uk

metadata.title: Cambs foodbank raises £15,000 after van stolen and stripped for parts
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridge City Foodbank has raised £15,000 in a week after its van was stolen and stripped for parts.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs foodbank raises £15,000 after van stolen and stripped for parts
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire foodbank charity has raised £15,000 in a week after its van was stolen and stripped for parts. Cambridge City Foodbank reached its fundraising target in less than a week after damage to one van put its operation at serious risk. Police were called at about 2.20pm on October 7 after a foodbank vehicle was reported stolen from Nuffield Close, Cambridge. Police recovered the vehicle in the early hours of October 8, but parts were missing. The foodbank's van was recovered but parts were missing (Image: Cambridge City Foodbank) A police spokesperson said: "Investigations are ongoing and anyone with any information or relevant dashcam or doorbell footage is urged to report this to police." Cambridge City Foodbank provides emergency and affordable food to people in need, using vans to transport donations and food parcels. The independent charity launched an appeal for a replacement vehicle, saying the incident put its operation "at serious risk". But people across Cambridgeshire rallied behind the foodbank, which exceeded its £15,000 target in less than a week. Stephen Thornton, Chair of Trustees at the foodbank, said: "When our van was stolen, we were at real risk of our operations grinding to a halt, and not being able to provide food for the people in Cambridge who needed it. The foodbank hit their fundraising target of £15,000 in just a week (Image: Cambridge City Foodbank) "But what happened next has left everyone at Cambridge City Foodbank both humbled and inspired. "We have been absolutely blown away by the response to what was a tragic and heart-breaking situation and, in less than a week, our appeal has hit our target of £15,000." The charity can now source a replacement van and continue providing food for people in need. The charity called the situation "tragic and heart-breaking" (Image: Cambridge City Foodbank) The charity said further donations through its JustGiving page would support the foodbank’s wider work. Mr Thornton added: "Every single donation, whatever its size, has made a huge difference to our charity and every person we serve and, while words can’t really express the sense of gratitude we have for your incredible support, as Chair of Trustees, I extend my sincere thanks to each and every one of you."
