metadata.title: Navy sailor accused of plotting to leak intelligence to Russia appears in court
metadata.contentSnippet: A Royal Navy sailor accused of plotting to leak classified information to Russia has appeared in court.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Navy sailor accused of plotting to leak intelligence to Russia appears in court
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Royal Navy sailor accused of plotting to leak classified information to Russia has appeared in court for the first time. Teddy Young, 24, is alleged to have abused his high-level security clearance to access secret defence and intelligence data after being deployed on a Navy vessel. It is said he had drafted a message in Russian containing classified information and had allegedly taken steps to make direct contact with the Russian authorities. Young, who lives in a semi-detached house in the village of Clapham, on the outskirts of Bedford, appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday to face the charges for the first time. "The allegation is that while serving as a Royal Navy warfare intelligence rating with high-level security clearance and intelligence-system access, Teddy Stanley Greenidge Young accessed and retained sensitive UK defence and intelligence material and engaged in activity consistent with preparing to pass protected information to a foreign power," the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) told the court in a written summary of the allegations. It is said Young, who joined the Navy in April 2024, committed the offences on his first deployment, which began on November 4, 2024. He is accused of using the dark web to try to make contact with Russian authorities, drafting a message which "sought to make contact with a potential threat actor", and breaking Navy rules by copying information to a private email account. Young wore a grey sweatshirt and joggers as he appeared in the dock in front of District Judge Annabel Pilling. He was arrested by counter-terror police at his home in Bedfordshire on Tuesday, having previously been arrested in Hampshire last year. He is charged with engaging in conduct preparatory to the commission of an offence under the National Security Act 2023 and a second allegation of obtaining, accepting or retaining material benefit from a designated body. According to the charges, it is said that between November 26, 2024 and May 21, 2025 Young "disclosed protected information for a purpose which he knew, or having regard to other matters known to him ought reasonably to have known, was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the UK intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power, engaged in conduct in preparation for the commission of such an act". Over the same six-month period, Young is said to have "obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power". Young was not asked to enter any pleas during the four-minute court hearing on Thursday. The judge told him: "As you know the matters that you have been charged with are too serious to be dealt with at this court and need to be dealt with at a crown court." Judge Pilling sent the case to the Old Bailey, where Young is due to appear on October 16, and remanded him in custody. When announcing the charge, police stressed there was no link between this investigation and the ongoing RAF Fairford probe. A Royal Navy spokesman said: "A member of the Royal Navy has been charged with National Security Act offences following an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing London. "As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage."

metadata.title: 'Calculated' man accepted neighbour's parcel before plotting burglary
metadata.contentSnippet: A man from Hemingford Grey who had been trusted to accept a delivery for his neighbour plotted a burglary when he realised their house was empty.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Calculated' man accepted neighbour's parcel before plotting burglary
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man who had been trusted to accept a delivery for his neighbour plotted a burglary when he realised their house was empty. Sam Biddle, 51, of Margetts, Hemingford Grey, accepted the delivery while his neighbour was away from home. After realising the property was unoccupied, he used that knowledge to plan a break-in. At 6.22pm, he left the parcel by the front door of the house. Later that evening, between 8.08pm and 9.35pm, Biddle returned to the address several times wearing gloves and a face covering. During the attempted burglary, he tried the front door and removed a CCTV camera. He also attempted to force open a side door and smashed a windowpane in an effort to gain entry. Police were called after the victim received notifications from the CCTV camera to his phone. Biddle was identified by detectives from the CCTV and arrested. At Peterborough Crown Court on October 1, Biddle was sentenced to two years and three months in prison. He admitted attempted burglary and activating a previous suspended sentence. Detective Sergeant Jonathan Lockwood said: "This was a calculated offence committed by someone who took advantage of a position of trust. "Having accepted a parcel on behalf of his neighbour, Biddle realised the property was empty and saw it as an opportunity to commit a burglary. "He returned repeatedly, concealing his identity and making determined efforts to get inside. "Thankfully, the home’s security system alerted the victim to what was happening, allowing offices to respond, leading to Biddle’s arrest." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk or newsdesk@huntspost.co.uk

metadata.title: Counter-terror police investigating after two men arrested at Cambs RAF base
metadata.contentSnippet: Counter terror police have launched an investigation after two men were arrested on suspicion of trespass offences at the RAF Molesworth base in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Counter-terror police investigating after two men arrested at Cambs RAF base
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Counter terror police have launched an investigation after two men were arrested on suspicion of trespass offences at an RAF base in Cambridgeshire. Security patrols by Ministry of Defence Police at RAF Molesworth identified an abandoned vehicle at 10pm on Wednesday (October 7). Officers from Cambridgeshire Constabulary also attended and carried out further searches of the area where a small breach in the perimeter fence was identified. At 2am the next day, two men, aged 36 and 32, were arrested inside the base perimeter. They were initially arrested on suspicion of trespass on a prohibited site and criminal damage and taken to a police station. The pair have since been further arrested on suspicion of an offence under section 4 of the National Security Act 2023. Both men remain in police custody at this time. Officers are carrying out two searches at addresses in the Peterborough area in connection with the investigation. The abandoned vehicle was recovered by police and taken to a nearby location. While undergoing further searches, concerns over the vehicle led to the deployment of specialist ‘EOD’ officers to carry out additional checks. As a precaution, a cordon was in place, which impacted on local roads in the Glatton area, including part of the A1(M). However, after assessment by specialist officers, nothing of concern was found and all cordons have since been lifted. The incident is now being investigated by officers from Counter Terrorism Policing. Commander Helen Flanagan, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: “We’re very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites, but at this stage there is nothing to suggest this incident is connected to the events at RAF Fairford last week. "Our investigation into this incident is at its very early stages. A big part of this is looking at any potential motivation as to why the men were present at the site, but I must stress we are keeping an open mind at this stage and enquiries are very much ongoing. "As ever, I would ask the public to remain vigilant and if you see anything of concern, then to contact police." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Prolific thief targeted shops and businesses including bakery
metadata.contentSnippet: A prolific thief who targeted shops and businesses, including Tesco and Co-op, across Cambridge has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Prolific thief targeted shops and businesses including bakery
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A prolific thief who targeted shops and businesses across Cambridge has been jailed. Jack Wilmot, of no fixed address, admitted a series of burglaries, thefts and assaults against shop workers over a two-week period. Between August 21 and September 4, he carried out repeated offences at shops where he climbed over the till area to take cigarettes and alcohol. On two occasions he assaulted members of staff. Wilmot also broke into Dorringtons Bakery and stole a charity box as well as breaking into Milton Road Pharmacy. The 29-year-old stole perfume, alcohol and meat worth almost £600 from Tesco, John Lewis, Co-op and Sainsbury’s. At Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on Friday (October 2), Wilmot was sentenced to a year in prison. He pleaded guilty to nine counts of burglary, two counts of common assault and four counts of theft. He was also handed a five-year Criminal Behaviour Order. This bans him from any Marks and Spencer, John Lewis, Co-op, Sainsbury’s or Tesco shop within the boundary of the A14, M11 and A11. Wilmot must pay a total of £2,469 in compensation to retailers Co-op, John Lewis, Sainsbury’s, Tesco as well as the victims he assaulted. Detective Constable Zoe Bramley, said: "Wilmot’s offending had a significant impact on retailers and their staff, who were repeatedly targeted over a short period of time. "His crime escalated from shop thefts to burglaries and assaults on shop workers carrying out their jobs. "This sentence, along with the Criminal Behaviour Order, demonstrates that persistent offending will not be tolerated and that we will continue to work with businesses to protect staff and bring people like Wilmot to justice" Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: Serving Royal Navy member charged with spying after Bedfordshire arrest
metadata.contentSnippet: A serving member of the Royal Navy has been charged with spying following an arrest in Bedfordshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Serving Royal Navy member charged with spying after Bedfordshire arrest
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A serving member of the Royal Navy has been charged with spying following his arrest in Bedfordshire. Teddy Young, 24, will appear in court on today (October 8) accused of obtaining protected information which could benefit a unnamed foreign power, the Metropolitan Police said. Young was arrested by counter-terror police at his home in Bedfordshire on Tuesday, having previously been arrested in Hampshire last year. He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court facing charges that between November 2024 and May 2025 he "engaged in conduct in preparation for committing an offence of disclosing protected information, contrary to section 18 of the National Security Act 2023". Between the same dates it is also alleged he "obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power, knowing or having regard to other matters known to him ought reasonably to know was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom, contrary to section 1 of the National Security Act 2023". Police stressed there was no link between this investigation and the ongoing RAF Fairford probe. Commander Helen Flanagan, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: "These are very serious charges against a serving member of the armed forces. We have worked extremely closely with relevant operational colleagues within the Ministry of Defence as our investigation has progressed to ensure appropriate measures could be taken to mitigate any potential risks linked to this matter." A Royal Navy spokesman said: "A member of the Royal Navy has been charged with National Security Act (NSA) offences following an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing London. As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage."

metadata.title: 'Violent' arsonist chased ex with hammer before starting fire outside her home
metadata.contentSnippet: A "violent" arsonist from Histon in Cambridgeshire who smashed up his ex-partner's home before chasing her with a hammer has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Violent' arsonist chased ex with hammer before starting fire outside her home
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A "violent" arsonist from Cambridgeshire who smashed up his ex-partner's home and chased her with a hammer has been jailed. Anthony Lamb, 51, showed up at his partner’s home in Histon, near Cambridge, on July 30 and began causing damage before trying to attack her with a hammer. The victim managed to escape to a nearby property and call police. When officers arrived, they discovered a fire had been started close to the victim’s front door. They managed to extinguish it and promptly arrested Lamb. Lamb, of Church Street, Gamlingay, pleaded guilty to two counts of criminal damage and breach of a restraining order. He was sentenced to a total of three years and six months in prison at Peterborough Crown Court on Thursday October 1. Detective Constable Jack Sillince, who investigated, said: "Lamb launched a violent and frightening attack against his ex-partner. "If she hadn’t escaped to her neighbour’s and if the fire had taken hold this could have been even worse. “I am glad justice has been done and hope Lamb reflects on his actions while behind bars." metadata.contentSnippet: Popular padel tennis company Pulse Padel is set to open a new venue in Peterborough in just a few weeks time.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New padel venue coming to Cambridgeshire - here's when
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A popular padel tennis company is set to open a new venue in Cambridgeshire in just a few weeks time. Pulse Padel will open four new padel courts at the Blue Diamond Garden Centre in Peterborough this autumn. The venue will have three covered doubles courts and one uncovered court. Beginners and experienced players are welcome. Pulse Padel said: "Whether you’re new to padel or already love the game, this will be the perfect venue for you." The exact opening date has not yet been confirmed, but Pulse Padel Peterborough will launch in November, the company confirmed on social media. Players can join Pulse Padel’s WhatsApp community through a QR code or social media link. Players have also been urged to download the Nettla app to be among the first to use the courts. The news comes after Pulse Padel Huntingdon launched at Blue Diamond Garden Centre in Banks End on August 29. A spokesman for Pulse Padel said that the response from the Huntingdon community had been "incredible". Padel tennis is widely regarded as the UK's fastest-growing racquet sport.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Plans have been submitted to install a permanent hot-food takeaway trailer in a Huntingdonshire village. Poopalasingam Thillaivarothayan is seeking permission to change the use of land at a property in Fenstanton for the food trailer. Application documents, submitted on September 25, say the trailer would be installed permanently on the applicant’s premises. The floor plan shows a trailer measuring about 4.5 metres by 2.4 metres, with fryers, hot plates, refrigeration units and preparation areas. The site would include outdoor storage for general waste, mixed recycling and food waste. The documents state that the containers would be kept closed to prevent odours and vermin and the storage area would be cleaned regularly. The application says contamination risks would be minimal because the food team would manage operational waste. It also says flood risk at the site is low. Noise would be reduced by servicing exhaust fans, using insulated or quieter commercial appliances and restricting operating hours. The measures are intended to limit disturbance to neighbouring properties. Full details on the plans can be found using the Huntingdonshire District Council planning portal, reference 26/01793/PRI032.

metadata.title: Further arrest as police continue to investigate 'violent disorder' in town
metadata.contentSnippet: Police have made another arrest after violent disorder on The Broadway in St Ives which left two men with serious injuries.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Further arrest as police continue to investigate 'violent disorder' in town
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Police have made another arrest after violent disorder in a Huntingdonshire town which left two men with serious injuries. Officers received multiple calls to The Broadway, in St Ives, on the evening of August 29, reporting violence and criminal damage in the town centre. Two men were taken to hospital where they were treated for serious but not life threatening injuries. Last month, Cambridgeshire Constabulary revealed six people had been arrested in connection with the incident. Two 19-year-old men, from Hartford and St Ives, were arrested on suspicion of a public order offence. A 20-year-old man from Huntingdon was arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and possession of drugs. A 29-year-old woman from Wyton was also arrested on suspicion of a public order offence. Meanwhile, a 19-year-old man from Whittlesey was arrested on suspicion of assault occasioning grievous bodily harm. They have all been bailed pending further enquiries and further arrests are expected in the coming weeks, the force confirmed. A sixth person, a man from Chatteris, was arrested on suspicion of a public order offence but has since been released without charge. In an update on Tuesday (October 6), a spokesperson confirmed a 17-year-old boy from Saffron Walden, in Essex, was arrested on suspicion of affray. He has since been released on bail until October 26, 2027. Detective Inspector Luke Pedlar said: "Our investigation has progressed quickly and we have already made a number of arrests, with further enquiries ongoing. "We are committed to identifying everyone involved and ensuring they are held accountable for their actions. "I would like to thank the community for their support so far and continue to urge anyone with information, footage or who witnessed the disorder to come forward and speak to us." Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Awards will spotlight sustainable workplaces and energy champions
metadata.contentSnippet: Meet the judges for the Sustainable Workplace of the Year and East of England Energy Ambassador categories at the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards 2027.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Awards will spotlight sustainable workplaces and energy champions
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: With innovators operating across multiple sectors, the East of England is playing a significant role in advancing sustainable business across the UK. This is what the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards are all about, and the Sustainable Workplace of the Year and East of England Energy Ambassador awards will spotlight the progressive, sustainable local organisations and people who are contributing to the region’s growing reputation. Here, the judges for these categories tell us more about what they’ll be looking for in the winners. James Groves, managing director of Indigo Swan (Image: Indigo Swan) Sponsored by Indigo Swan James Groves, managing director, Indigo Swan Why were you keen to get involved in the Clean & Green Awards? As a respected energy consultant in Norfolk, I felt it was important that Indigo Swan supported these awards and helped to bring attention to the amazing businesses across the region that are really making a statement when it comes to sustainability and net zero. What do you bring to the judging process? I bring more than 16 years’ experience within the energy sector, an understanding of the sustainable market and an ISO14001 accreditation. Through my experience at Indigo Swan – beginning as commercial director in 2018, becoming MD in 2019 and leading a management buyout in 2022 – I also have a clear understanding of how behavioural and cultural change in a business can impact your journey to being more sustainable and how important it will be on the journey to net zero. Have you ever been judged for an award yourself. If so, how will you use that experience when judging this award? Yes. The key for me is making sure that the award, if it’s for a company, is written by the company. We want to convey what the business does, stands for and is implementing. I want to see clear examples of where change has taken place. Statistics that can be proven and the understanding of change within an organisation are areas to focus on. I’ll also be looking for evidence of the impact on the people within the business and, of course, passion – all areas that have helped us with our success. What will you be looking for in the winner? A great combination of investment, behavioural change and a clear understanding of how being sustainable has helped to grow the business financially and improved the culture and engagement of the staff. The winner will show what best practice looks like, supported through facts, figures and accreditations. What advice would you give to anyone that’s considering entering? Do it. What do you have to lose? You have to buy a ticket to win the raffle. It will show your business as a shining light for how being more sustainable should be managed, and it will create a number of new opportunities. Ian Pease, business development manager at GENERATE (Image: Departure Lounge Media Group) Sponsored by GENERATE Ian Pease, business development manager, GENERATE Can you tell us a bit about your career to date? I am responsible for business development at OrbisEnergy, a clean energy business hub in Lowestoft, Suffolk. I have 25 years’ experience in the energy sector, during which time I’ve worked in both the public and private sectors in economic development, skills and competence, oil and gas, offshore wind, project management and business development. Part of my job is to manage GENERATE, established by local authorities in Norfolk, Suffolk and Essex to attract and support inward investment and business growth in the East of England’s energy sector. Why were you keen to get involved in the Clean & Green Awards? I wanted to get involved in these awards because I think it’s important for business leaders to be associated with such a high-profile awards programme and support the East Anglia Clean & Green initiative. What do you bring to the judging process? I’ve been in the energy sector for many years and have seen lots of new technologies come to the market. I’ve also seen firsthand how the composition of the East of England’s energy sector is changing, as it continues on its journey to a fully decarbonisation energy system. What will you be looking for in the winner? As the award category name suggests, I’ll be looking for a genuine ambassador for the East of England’s energy sector. In my opinion, the winner will be someone who’s making a difference and driving our region’s energy sector in a positive direction. What advice would you give to anyone that’s considering entering? My advice for entrants is to take time with your application and make sure you include all the good work you’re doing and your plans for the future, too. The deadline for entries to the East Anglia Clean & Green Awards is November 8 at midnight. For more information or to enter, visit cleanandgreenawards.co.uk

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire man pleads guilty to defrauding woman out of £126k
metadata.contentSnippet: A Soham man has pleaded guilty to defrauding a woman out of a six-figure sum.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire man pleads guilty to defrauding woman out of £126k
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire man has pleaded guilty to defrauding a woman out of a six-figure sum. Kambiz Akhondi appeared at Peterborough Crown Court on Tuesday (October 6) after being charged with fraud by abuse of position. The 60-year-old initially pleaded not guilty but changed this after the judge indicated he would not face more than three years in prison if he changed his plea. His defence had sought a Goodyear indication, which allows the judge to tell a defendant what the maximum sentence will be before they plead guilty. Akhondi, of Calfe Fen Close, Soham, was accused of transferring sums amounting to around £126k from Maud Miller’s bank account to his own. The offence happened between October 24, 2018, and March 17, 2020, while he was in a position of power over her finances. The court heard that Akhondi was expected to safeguard her estate and not act against her financial interests, but transferred the sums for his own gain. Akhondi was released on unconditional bail and is due to reappear in court to be sentenced on November 18.

Joshua Liddle, of Shapland Close, Huntingdon, is set to appear at Peterborough Magistrates' Court for a sentencing hearing on Wednesday (October 7). He was convicted of nine separate offences, which occurred between April 23 and 24 this year, at a separate hearing, court listings show. metadata.contentSnippet: A Southern barbecue restaurant Hickory's Smokehouse is set to open a new restaurant in Cambridge next week.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: New Southern barbecue smokehouse restaurant to open in Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A new Southern barbecue smokehouse restaurant is set to open in Cambridgeshire. Hickory’s Smokehouse, on Milton Road in Cambridge, will open its doors on October 16 and promises to deliver classic American barbecue and Southern hospitality in a family-friendly setting. The restaurant, known for its low-and-slow smoked meats and laid-back atmosphere, will open in the former Milton Arms pub. A statement from Hickory’s reads: "We're preparing to show our unique take on Southern Hospitality to you, the good people of Cambridge & beyond! "We can’t wait to welcome you for smokin’ BBQ, shakin’ drinks & some good old-fashioned Southern Hospitality!" The Cambridge smokehouse will be the second Hickory's location in the county, alongside the restaurant in Hampton, Peterborough, which opened on June 19. The menu will feature smokehouse favourites such as Memphis ribs and 16-hour smoked Texas-style brisket, all prepared by Hickory’s team of trained pitmasters using smokers imported from Tennessee and Missouri. Guests can watch the pitmasters at work from the chef’s bar. The restaurant includes a secluded garden and two covered terraces. Seating ranges from cosy tables for small groups to larger spaces for celebrations and family gatherings. The restaurant also features a dedicated kids’ menu, table-top activities, and a movie room. The children's menu will offer dishes such as Pan Cakes, Mac 'n' Cheese, Popcorn Chicken Bites and burgers. The Fro-Co Creation Station lets children (and adults) create their own desserts using Hickory’s signature frozen custard. The bar will serve a wide selection of cocktails, craft beers, and more than 25 bourbons, alongside a mix of non-alcoholic options including mocktails, sodas, and sweet teas. Sports fans can catch the action on multiple screens throughout the bar area. Bookings are now open for Hickory’s Cambridge restaurant ahead of its October 16 launch.

metadata.title: 'Awesome' Roman cremation urn and ploughshare found at Cambridgeshire dig
metadata.contentSnippet: An 'awesome' cremation urn was the big find at an archaeological dig in Cambridgeshire, which was a new attempt to locate a Roman villa.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Awesome' Roman cremation urn and ploughshare found at Cambridgeshire dig
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An 'awesome' cremation urn was the big find at an archaeological dig in Cambridgeshire, which was a new attempt to locate a Roman villa. Run by DigVentures, the two-week excavation was crowdfunded, with some of those donating working alongside professional archaeologists to find out more about the site, located in the countryside close to Sacrewell, on the outskirts of Peterborough. In the 1970s, archaeologists found remains of a winged Roman villa, including furnaces, painted plaster and tiled floors, but never uncovered the villa itself. The ploughshare was found alongside the glass cremation urn.. (Image: Jacob Reader) Fifty years on Nat Jackson, site director, and his team from DigVentures set about unearthing more of the villa's story, and that of the people who lived there, and also to make a fresh attempt to locate it. In two weeks, they excavated three trenches and found pottery, coins, roof tiles, underfloor-heating tiles, snail and oyster shells and, most excitingly, the cremation burial. The excavators found a blue glass urn in the remains of a wooden box, alongside an iron ploughshare - the cutting or leading edge of a plough. Reporter Sarah Cliss joined the DigVentures team for the last day of the dig. (Image: Sarah Cliss) Nat believes it could have belonged to someone who lived in the villa and perhaps farmed the land. "It is possible the person thought, 'I am a farmer; I want to be buried with farming tools', that's so cool, and it's a really awesome thing to find. I have never found anything like it before," he said. It was Nat's job to draw up the specifics for the dig, researching as much as he could about the site and determining where the exploration trenches should go. Geophysical surveys have been carried out of the site to help locate the site of the Roman villa and the best place to dig exploration trenches. (Image: Jacob Reader) Geophysical surveys of the site also helped with that, and there were high hopes of finding a furnace in one of the trenches, which had shown a large iron deposit, but digging showed it was a false alarm when a large iron horseshoe was discovered. “It was massive, probably from a shire horse or something like that dating to the 18th century or 19th century, but it was not what we were hoping to find,” said Nat. Harriet Tatton, senior project officer for project development at DigVentures, was equally excited by the burial find. Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) She said the urn's hexagonal shape had helped to date it to around the 2nd century AD - so 1,800 years ago, give or take 100 years - so around the Antonine period or possibly to the time of the Emperor Flavian. The urn’s contents will be excavated carefully off-site in the hope of revealing more about the person buried inside. It is easy to make assumptions that it was a man because the person was buried with a ploughshare, but it could be a female and if we are lucky, we might be able to discover which. Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Harriet said it was common for people to be buried with objects that meant something to the people in life, but it should be remembered that the choices would most likely have been made by their family, not by the person themselves. Some of the volunteers were sponsored to join the dig through the online adult learning App Nibble, which also allowed me to join the fun for the day. Like the many other volunteers working alongside the professionals, I was given a trowel, a brush and bucket and set to work cleaning the stones of earth in one of the excavation ditches. Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) The aim was to reveal the natural geology of the area and to show the ditches that had been dug by the Roman occupiers of the site, ready for detailed work off-site. The other volunteers came from across the country; some had donated to the crowdfunding appeal, while others had received the dig as a gift. One man, who was a huge fan of Channel 4's Time Team hosted by Tony Robinson, had always dreamed of joining a dig and had been given the chance as a 60th birthday present from his wife. Volunteers and professionals worked side by side to unearth the secrets buried at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Another had received it as a retirement gift. Both thoroughly enjoyed getting stuck in and were excited when they unearthed a piece of roof tile. One woman from Leicestershire was delighted that she had been given a chance to help unearth the urn. “I can't believe I got to work on something so precious. I told my family not to tell the team just how clumsy I can be, as I didn't want to miss out; it was so special,” she said. Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Another man from Kent said it had reawakened an old passion, and that it was wonderful to pull a piece of history out of the ground and hold it in his hand. Harriet said all the finds would be cleaned, examined and catalogued. The urn, ploughshare and coins could go to a museum, while less significant items may be reburied. Nat and his team are planning to return next September when they hope to excavate in an adjoining field, where they hope to finally discover the location of the villa. "We can't wait to come back, and hopefully find ourselves a Roman villa," he said, "that would be the dream."on site, Site director Nat Jackson carefully handles the iron ploughshare unearthed at the site. (Image: Jacob Reader) Site director Nat Jackson talks to the volunteers about the one of the trenches. (Image: Jacob Reader) Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Site director Nat Jackson leads a tour of the site. (Image: Jacob Reader) Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) The finds will be carefully cleaned, examined and catalogued. (Image: Jacob Reader) Volunteers worked alongside professional archaeologists at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) Volunteers and professionals worked side by side to unearth the secrets buried at the site near Sacrewell. (Image: Jacob Reader) A team from the adult online learning App Nibble were also on site having sponsored some people to join the dig. They had travelled from Ukraine to join the excavation. (Image: Jacob Reader) The site forms part of the Nene Valley, a major Roman centre of production, transport and trade that included villa estates, pottery kilns and ironworking facilities.

metadata.title: School responds after inspection uncovers fire safety 'deficiencies'
metadata.contentSnippet: Longsands Academy in St Neots, which is run by the Astrea Academy Trust, has reassured parents after several "deficiencies" were unearthed during a recent fire safety inspection.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: School responds after inspection uncovers fire safety 'deficiencies'
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A school in Huntingdonshire has reassured parents after "deficiencies" were unearthed during a recent fire safety inspection. Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service visited Longsands Academy, in St Neots, at the end of September, it has been revealed. In a letter seen by The Hunts Post, the inspection was organised to assess concerns raised about the safety of the premises. Fire safety officers unearthed several deficiencies under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005. It comes after two sources approached this newspaper to raise concerns about fire safety at Longsands, which is run by the Astrea Academy Trust. The school has since confirmed it is working to resolve the issues, which include a defective fire alarm sounder and a damaged set of fire doors. Inspectors raised concerns about a set of fire safety doors in N Block (Image: Supplied) In a letter to parents, the school said the site is "considered to be safe and complies overwhelmingly" with required fire safety standards. It added: "The inspection highlighted one or two minor deficiencies which our site team is now working on to resolve. "The fire safety inspectors found that the fire alarm sounder in H Block is faulty, due to a defect on the fire panel, and that some emergency lighting is not working properly. "They also said that two fire-resisting doors in N Block needed to be repaired, after some damage was caused. "However, the inspectors are satisfied that we are working to put these issues right and do not feel the need to re-inspect the school." Longsands Academy revealed the fire doors had been damaged (Image: Supplied) It continues: "I would like to take this opportunity to remind parents and carers of the important role families play in supporting Longsands’ approach to appropriate student behaviour. "In recent weeks, some damage has been caused to school property by students and we would ask you to reinforce at home the expectations we have around respect and responsibility." A spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service confirmed officers "arranged for a further visit at the end of September." They added: "A minor deficiencies notice was issued to the Responsible Person, which was focussed on routine maintenance issues. "The Responsible Person has been fully engaged in the process and proactive in addressing the highlighted deficiencies." Have you got a story you want to share? summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Police have cordoned off Camp Beagle, a permanent protest outside a controversial puppy breeding facility in Cambridgeshire. Officers are stationed outside the entrance to MBR Acres in Wyton, Huntingdon, this evening (October 6) and a police cordon has been established around Camp Beagle. The circumstances around what has happened are not yet clear. Last week, police were called to the facility last week, at 11.10pm on September 29, after reports of a burglary. A 43-year-old woman from Inverness was arrested after reports of a "burglary" where "a number of dogs" were taken, police said. It has not been confirmed if the police presence and cordon is linked to this incident. Camp Beagle, the UK's longest-running permanent animal rights protest camp, has maintained a continuous presence outside MBR Acres since the summer of 2021. Camp Beagle is stationed outside MBR Acres in Huntingdon (Image: Newsquest) The organisation demands that the facility close and end the use of beagles for research purposes. MBR Acres said that their lawful role is to breed and supply healthy dogs for regulated scientific research. However, there have been multiple protests against the facility, including one on September 26 which saw more than 200 march in protest against the breeding of beagles at the site.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Thousands of crime victims in Cambridgeshire will benefit from £4.4 million in Government funding. The money, allocated to the Cambridgeshire Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC), will fund practical, emotional, and therapeutic support over the next two years for people affected by all types of crime, including domestic abuse and sexual violence. Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones visited the PCC’s Victim and Witness Hub and Peterborough Women’s Aid services on September 30, to meet survivors and see the impact of the specialist support services. Ms Davies-Jones said: "Meeting victim-survivors today and hearing first-hand about their experiences has been incredibly powerful. "I want to thank the dedicated staff behind these life-changing services, helping people recover from trauma, rebuild their confidence and move forwards. "That’s why we’re continuing to back these vital services as we work to tackle violence against women and girls and deliver swifter justice for victims." The funding is part of a wider £550 million Government investment over three years to support victims and witnesses throughout the justice process. An additional £18.9 million is being invested in further support services, including a new national helpline.

metadata.title: Mayor warns devolved power over water services ‘a bit bonkers’
metadata.contentSnippet: Andy Burnham’s plan to give regional leaders more power over water utilities “frankly, is a bit bonkers”, Paul Bristow has warned.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Mayor warns devolved power over water services ‘a bit bonkers’
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Andy Burnham’s plan to give regional leaders more power over water utilities “frankly, is a bit bonkers”, a mayor has warned. Paul Bristow claimed mayoral devolution in England was a “success story” for his party, the Conservatives, but warned it was “not going to solve all our problems”. Devolution has been a central plank of Mr Burnham’s governing agenda since he became Labour leader and Prime Minister earlier this year. During his first week in Downing Street, the former Greater Manchester mayor hosted regional leaders – including mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Mr Bristow – at his new No 10 North in Manchester. Asked whether cross-party efforts to work on mayoral devolution could continue, Mr Bristow told the Press Association that the Government’s “message is good”. He said: “We want that responsibility, that accountability, but we need the resources that come with it.” The Prime Minister last week promised mayors “will have new powers to hold water companies to account, with tougher consequences for those which repeatedly fail”, as part of a bid to “strengthen public control” over the sector. Mr Burnham more widely pledged “more power and control over the basics”, which he said would be “in the hands of people and places to set their own ambitions”. Attending the Conservative Party conference in Birmingham, Mr Bristow said: “The idea that I’m going to become responsible for a water company or Anglian Water, I think, frankly, is a bit bonkers.” He added devolution was “about the market, and it’s about Government, and it’s about institutions like the universities working together” on regional priorities. He also said: “I think the water companies want to be responsible to their shareholders, don’t they? They’re a private organisation. “So, it’s about having the right devolution in the right places.” Mr Bristow said: “Devolution is just not a means for growth itself. “You can’t just say devolution is going to solve all our problems. “It’s not going to solve the problems associated with defence, it’s not going to solve the problems associated with welfare – the fact we’re paying more on welfare than we raise in income tax. “It’s not going to solve some of these big fundamental state-led issues, but what it can do is deliver growth in targeted areas.” Asked about the Conservatives’ approach towards devolution, Mr Bristow said he wanted to see his party “back what works”. He added: “Kemi Badenoch, I’m sure, will understand that English devolution is a Conservative success story.” Several regional mayoralties were set up under the Conservative government, including Cambridgeshire and Peterborough in 2017. In the same year, Mr Burnham became the first mayor of Greater Manchester, a role he held for just over nine years. In the English Devolution White Paper, published during former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer’s premiership, the Government set out its ambition for everywhere in the country to have a strategic authority, such as a mayor-led body.

metadata.title: More than 60 babies remembered in St Ives memorial ribbon display
metadata.contentSnippet: A town councillor has organised St Ives’ first baby loss memorial ribbon display.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: More than 60 babies remembered in St Ives memorial ribbon display
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A town councillor has organised St Ives’ first baby loss memorial ribbon display. The event is being held to support families and break the silence around pregnancy and baby loss. A St Ives Town Councillor, who has experienced miscarriage herself, launched the memorial in St Ives after hearing from local mothers who wanted a way to remember their babies closer to home. St Ives Town Bridge will be illuminated pink and blue (Image: St Ives Town Council) She said: "Until 2024, our town had nothing to commemorate Baby Loss Awareness Week, and as a mother who has miscarried a child myself, and having surveyed local mums who said they can't drive miles to another town for baby loss week, I felt I just had to do something to remember our beautiful babies." "This will be the third year running, and like the last two years, local businesses all come together and do a lovely pink and blue display in their shop windows in support too, so the whole high street has scattered pink and blue, with some shops and pubs lighting up their own buildings pink and blue too." The memorial aims to support families affected by baby loss. (Image: St Ives Town Council) A ribbon memorial will be displayed outside St Ives Methodist Church from October 9 to 15, with more than 60 babies already named in previous years, some dating as far back as 1975. Ribbons and markers will be available for visitors to write messages in memory of their babies. Donations are welcome for Sands Baby Loss Charity, though not required. Pink and blue ribbons will commemorate babies who have died (Image: St Ives Town Council) She said: "Having lost a baby myself, its the recognition that really counts, it says that you are seen, that it is a real loss, not 'just one of those things,' and officiates it." The St Ives Town Bridge will also be illuminated in pink and blue throughout the week, a gesture that last year sparked conversations and raised awareness across the community. All are welcome to visit the display, regardless of age, gender, religion, or the length of time since their loss.

metadata.title: Teens who left man with fractured skull in unprovoked attack avoid jail
metadata.contentSnippet: Two teenagers who left a man with a fractured skull in an unprovoked attack in Market Square, Cambridge, have been sentenced.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Teens who left man with fractured skull in unprovoked attack avoid jail
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two teenagers who left a man with a fractured skull in an unprovoked attack in Cambridgeshire have been sentenced. The 20-year-old victim was approached by two teenage girls in Market Square, in Cambridge, on August 12, 2024, and asked to buy them alcohol. When he refused, the girls became aggressive, with one repeatedly hitting him with her slipper. As the situation escalated, more teenagers gathered around the victim, leaving him cornered against a spiked metal fence near St Mary’s Church. During the attack, Xavier Matelot launched a flying kick to the side of the victim’s head, causing it to strike the metal fence. Zein Gibril then repeatedly punched him before the group dispersed. The victim was taken to Addenbrooke’s Hospital, where he was treated for a skull fracture and a bleed on the brain. Sentencing the pair at Cambridge Crown Court on September 25, the Judge described the group that surrounded and attacked the victim as behaving like ‘a pack of wolves’. Gibril, 18, of Cavendish Avenue, Cambridge, was handed an 18 month Youth Rehabilitation Order after admitting causing grievous bodily harm without intent and possession of cannabis. He must also complete 100 hours of unpaid work. Matelot, 19, of Briar Way, Peterborough, was sentenced to 21 months imprisonment, suspended for two years, after admitting inflicting grievous bodily harm without intent. He must complete 120 hours of unpaid work. Detective Constable Luca Bellomo, who investigated, said: “This was a shocking and entirely unprovoked attack on a young man in broad daylight. "The victim suffered serious injuries and as a result has been left with potentially life changing injuries. "Violence of this nature has no place in our communities." metadata.title: Cambridgeshire farmer warns environmental progress at risk after £150k funding loss
metadata.contentSnippet: A Cambridgeshire farmer has warned that environmental progress could be lost after missing out on vital funding.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire farmer warns environmental progress at risk after £150k funding loss
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire farmer has warned that environmental progress could be lost after missing out on vital funding. Peter Hatley, NFU Cambridge branch chair and a third-generation farmer from Landbeach, was unable to secure support through the Government’s Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) scheme. The scheme, which encourages environmentally friendly farming practices, closed just six hours after opening on September 22, leaving many farmers without access to funding. Mr Hatley said: "All the work that has been done to support wildlife and the environment here will need to be ripped up. "We are left with no choice but to farm intensively as a business so I can look after my family and look after my business." He and his adviser encountered technical problems with the application portal and by the time they reached the Rural Payments Agency for support, the funds had already been exhausted. Mr Hatley said: "We were hoping for £150,000 over three years, which is a monumental amount of money for us to lose. "I don’t know what we’re going to do now. "I don’t want to have to rip everything up, and if we had any clarity about when SFI 27 is going to open it would make decision making much easier." His family has farmed the land for nearly 100 years, and they have taken part in environmental schemes for two decades. He said: "Without this funding, nature won’t pay the bills and we will be left with no choice but to undo much of what we’ve spent so long working to achieve." The NFU has repeatedly called on the government to expand the SFI budget. By 4pm the government confirmed that the 2026 SFI scheme was closed for applications, with the entire budget allocated.

metadata.title: Amazing photos and video show the Red Arrows soaring over Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: Amazing photos and footage show the Red Arrows soaring over Cambridgeshire and Fenland in their last public display of the year at IWM Duxford.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Amazing photos and video show the Red Arrows soaring over Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Amazing photos and footage show the Red Arrows soaring over Cambridgeshire in their last public display of the year. The Red Arrows took to the Cambridgeshire skies on Saturday (October 3) as part of their final public appearance of the year at the Flying Finale event at IWM Duxford. The display ended the airshow season and marked Wing Commander Jon Bond’s final performance as Red 1 after three years as team leader. The Red Arrows put on a show-stopping display Their final public appearance of the year was at IWM Duxford in Cambridgeshire The team endured a challenging year, flying seven jets instead of its usual nine because of parts shortages affecting its ageing BAE Systems Hawk T1s. The jets have been in service since 1980 and are due to retire in 2030. The Red Arrows have had a challenging year after going from nine jets to seven This was the last appearance of the year for the Red Arrows The Red Arrows also completed a month-long tour of the United States for its 250th birthday celebrations. They were then stranded in Canada for several weeks after poor weather stopped them returning to the UK. The RAF grounded all Hawk aircraft on September 24 after a training accident in Wales, but has since cleared them to fly. Fans in Cambridgeshire had another chance to see the team in action the day before the Duxford display. People turned out to Duxford to watch the air show On Friday, October 2, the Red Arrows made an 18-minute transit flight from RAF Waddington to RAF Mildenhall, passing over parts of the county. Footage by Daniel Hopper shows the jets soaring over the Fenland. The Red Arrows entered Cambridgeshire airspace around 2pm, north-west of Wisbech, before flying over Chatteris. They then flew over Mepal, Wilburton and Stretham before landing in Suffolk.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Woman set fire to deodorant can in attempted arson attack on neighbour
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire woman who set fire to a deodorant can and put it through her neighbour's letterbox in an attempted arson attack has been jailed. Beatrice Elliott, 31, was involved in a dispute with her neighbours in Chatteris in the early hours of 14 April. In response, she approached their front door, lit the can and put it through the letterbox. The fire didn’t spread and was put out by a man in the property. Police attended and Elliott, of Barley Close, Chatteris, was arrested. On Friday (October 2) at Cambridge Crown Court she was jailed for 16 months having admitted attempted arson at a previous hearing. PC Boots said: “Elliott’s behaviour that night was completely reckless. "This incident could have been far worse. Luckily, the fire didn’t spread, and nobody was injured.” Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Trial of former Cambridgeshire councillor charged with sexual offences to begin
metadata.contentSnippet: The trial of a former Peterborough City Councillor accused of rape and other sexual offences is due to begin today.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Trial of former Cambridgeshire councillor charged with sexual offences to begin
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The trial of a former Cambridgeshire councillor accused of rape and other sexual offences is due to begin today. Rylan Ray, 25, of Westgate, Peterborough, faces charges including rape and offences involving sexual activity with children. The charges arose while he was still a serving Peterborough city councillor. He is due to appear at Ipswich Crown Court today, October 5, with the trial scheduled to run until October 30. Ray, who was elected as a Conservative councillor for the Eye, Thorney and Newborough ward in 2022, was charged in 2025 with one count of rape, one of sexual activity with a child under 16 and two of causing a child under 16 to engage in sexual activity. He was also charged with six counts of causing a child to watch a sexual act, three of sexual assault and four of sexual communication with a child. Additional charges included four counts of causing or inciting a child to engage in sexual activity, three counts of making an indecent image of children, and one count of possessing prohibited images of children. He was also accused of possessing extreme pornographic images. Ray is no longer a serving councillor following elections at Peterborough City Council in May 2026.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire residents asked to shape council spending priorities through survey
metadata.contentSnippet: People are being invited to have their say on future spending priorities in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire residents asked to shape council spending priorities through survey
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: People are being invited to have their say on future spending priorities in Cambridgeshire. Cambridgeshire County Council has launched a public engagement survey to gather feedback on its upcoming business plan and budget for 2027–28, which will also include its medium-term financial strategy through to 2029–30. The survey asks residents to share their views on where the council should prioritise spending and savings in the years ahead. Lucy Nethsingha, leader of Cambridgeshire County Council, said: "Every year, the council has to set our business plan and a balanced budget, which is increasingly challenging as demand for services grows and costs continue to rise. "Despite these challenges, over recent years the council has provided much-needed stability in an increasingly uncertain world, and we remain in a stronger financial position than many councils across the country. "We are not immune to the significant cost and demand pressures faced by local government and must make careful decisions about how we use the finite resources available to us. "It is so important that residents have their say so that we can better understand what matters most to people and the priorities they believe are important for the Council. "Your feedback will help inform our business planning and budget-setting process, as councillors consider how best to plan and fund our services for the years ahead. "We hope as many residents as possible will take part in the survey, making their voices heard and informing future decisions about the council’s services across Cambridgeshire." The majority of day-to-day spending is required to support children's and adult social care, education and SEND, with the remainder used to maintain the highways network and deliver community-based services, including libraries and registration services. The engagement survey will be in two phases, with Phase 1 closing on 15 November 2026. To take part, visit Your Voice on the Cambridgeshire County Council website.

metadata.title: 'Drug driving' arrest after woman and girl seriously injured in crash
metadata.contentSnippet: A man has been arrested after a crash which seriously injured a woman and teenage girl on Bullock Road near Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Drug driving' arrest after woman and girl seriously injured in crash
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man has been arrested after a crash which seriously injured a woman and teenage girl near Peterborough. Police were called at 8.22am on Sunday (October 4) to Bullock Road, at its junction with Washingley Road, near Lutton. The collision involved a silver Vauxhall Astra and a silver Renault Scenic, Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed. The driver of the Scenic, a woman in her 50s, and her passenger, a teenage girl, both from Yaxley, were rushed to hospital with serious but not life-threatening injuries. Meanwhile, the driver of the Astra, a 31-year-old man from Lincoln, sustained minor injuries. He was arrested at the scene on suspicion of drug driving and causing serious injury by dangerous driving. He has since been released on bail to return to Thorpe Wood Police Station on December 30. Officers are appealing for information and dashcam footage from anyone who witnessed the collision or saw either vehicle in the moments leading up to it. Those with with information should contact police via the force website, quoting 35/NT/19967/26. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk or newsdesk@peterboroughmatters.co.uk

metadata.title: Former Cambridgeshire County Council Green Group leader resigns from party
metadata.contentSnippet: The former leader of the Green Group on Cambridgeshire County Council has resigned from the Green Party.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Former Cambridgeshire County Council Green Group leader resigns from party
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The former leader of the Green Group on Cambridgeshire County Council has resigned from the Green Party. Cllr Elliot Tong, who is also a Cambridge City councillor, said he no longer feels the party will allow him to stand up for what’s right. He led the group on the county council until May of this year, after first being elected to represent Abbey Ward in 2025. He has also represented Abbey on the city council since 2023 and was previously the Green Group’s deputy leader on the city council. Cllr Tong confirmed he will continue to sit as an independent councillor on both councils. He said he had become increasingly disillusioned with the party, who he said had pushed back against building council housing and his support for Palestine. In a statement released on Friday (October 2), he said: “Today, I’ve resigned from The Green Party, as well as the Green Group on both the city and county council. “I entered politics because I wanted to stand up for what’s right. I no longer feel that the Cambridge and South Cambridgeshire Green Party will allow me to do this. “Locally, my Green colleagues have pushed back against council housing in their own wards. “I have been threatened for standing up for Palestinians and told that doing so is unimportant. “Behind the scenes, I have been mocked for my neurodivergence. My loyalty will always be towards doing what’s right, not what’s convenient. “I am excited to continue standing up for regular people across Cambridge.” The two Green Group leaders on the city council, Cllr Sefira Davison and county council, Cllr Darren Green, issued a joint statement in response to the resignation which they said came as a “disappointment and a shock”. They said: “As we’re currently away at party conference at present, we don’t have all the facts on the ground. “Our feeling at present is that in our time in politics, we have come to know Elliot as a campaigner, a colleague, and a friend. “To hear from Elliot that he no longer felt able to stand as a Green was a disappointment and a shock. “We want to go on record first as saying that any form of harassment or discrimination is not acceptable to us, nor compatible with Green values. It should not be acceptable to anyone. “Elliot has been a steadfast colleague and a tireless councillor. His energy, enthusiasm, and support will be missed, and we hope to continue working together for the good of residents on both councils.

news.title: Ramsey Ward Councillor Arrested Over Alleged False Election Statements
news.summary: Ryan Coogan, a Reform UK councillor representing Ramsey Ward on Huntingdonshire District Council, was arrested on September 24 on suspicion of making false statements in election nomination papers. He has been released on bail and is due to return to Milton Police Station on December 22 as the investigation continues.
news.content: Reform councillor arrested over alleged false statements in election papers A Reform UK council group leader in Cambridgeshire has been arrested on suspicion of making false statements in election nomination papers. Representing the Ramsey Ward, Ryan Coogan was elected to Huntingdonshire District Council in the local elections on May 7. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed a man was arrested on September 24 on suspicion of making false statements in nomination papers. The 42-year-old from Waterbeach has since been released on bail to return to Milton Police Station on December 22. Coogan told The Hunts Post he has "worked and will continue to work with the police as part of the investigation". It comes after the force revealed it had launched an investigation into the alleged false statements shortly after the May election. A spokesperson said the inquiry relates to Coogan and the most recent election, though it has not disclosed the nature of the alleged statements. At the time, a spokesperson for Huntingdonshire District Council said: "We are aware of a police referral in relation to the recent district council elections. "As this matter is a live investigation, it would not be appropriate for the council or the returning officer to comment further at this stage." Coogan previously ran as Reform UK's candidate in the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough mayoral election, coming second last year. He was among the party's first representatives on the district council, winning his seat along with two other Reform candidates to represent the Ramsey ward. According to the Electoral Commission the penalties for a false statement on a nomination paper in England and Wales include an unlimited fine or up to one year in prison.
